help.openadapt-flow:
usage: openadapt-flow [-h] [--version] {command} ...

Record a task and compile it into a program that runs on this computer. With a record check
configured, a governed run confirms each save by reading the record back, and a run that can't
confirm a save stops and asks a person. When the screen changes, it finds the same field again or
stops, and a lasting fix needs a person's approval.

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --version   Show the version and exit

commands:
  {command}
    demo      Try the demonstration and tutorial
    verify    Check effects, receipts, and evidence
    record    Record a task and its narration
    teach     Teach a correction to a stopped workflow
    compile   Compile and prepare workflow bundles
    run       Run, resume, and route workflows
    approve   Review and approve paused work
    undo      Declare and run approved undo steps
    qualify   Qualify a workflow for its intended use
    repair    Review, test, and promote repairs
    inspect   Inspect workflows, runs, and reports
    workflow  Manage reusable workflow libraries
    services  Run local services and connectors
    setup     Configure connections, privacy, and access
    research  Run benchmarks and research tools

New here? Run 'openadapt-flow demo' to see a checked run and a stopped run side by side on one
page.

help.openadapt-flow approve:
usage: openadapt-flow approve [-h] [--approver APPROVER] [--resolution RESOLUTION]
                              [--authorize-uncertain-retry] [--approver-key APPROVER_KEY]
                              [--key-dir KEY_DIR] [--approver-root HEX]
                              run_dir

positional arguments:
  run_dir               The paused run directory (holds the escalation)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --approver APPROVER   Optional check: the approver id the --approver-key must be registered as.
                        The approval names the key's registered approver
  --resolution RESOLUTION
                        The chosen resolution (defaults to the pause's first proposed option) —
                        recorded for the audit trail
  --authorize-uncertain-retry
                        After reconciling an uncertain delivery, explicitly authorize one retry of
                        the possibly dispatched step (ordinary approval refuses)
  --approver-key APPROVER_KEY
                        The person's encrypted approver key (jit keygen; on the approver roster
                        via jit approver init or add). Its passphrase comes from
                        OPENADAPT_JIT_KEY_PASSPHRASE. A person's approval is signed with it;
                        without it the approval is refused
  --key-dir KEY_DIR     Key directory with the approver roster (default $OPENADAPT_JIT_KEY_DIR or
                        ~/.openadapt/jit)
  --approver-root HEX   The root approver key (64 hex) this run trusts: a person's answer counts
                        only when its signer is on the signed approver roster this key vouches
                        for. Also set by the deployment config's approvers.root_public_key or
                        OPENADAPT_APPROVER_ROOT; without one, a person's answer is refused

usage: openadapt-flow compile [-h] --out OUT --name NAME [--accept-params NAME1,NAME2]
                              [--params-from FILE] [--no-confirm-params] [--pixel-verify-enabled]

                        names fail loud.
  --params-from FILE    Non-interactive confirm pass: JSON decision file mapping each proposed
                        name to {"action": "confirm"|"rename"|"secret"|"constant", "name": "<new

help.openadapt-flow compile-agent:
usage: openadapt-flow compile-agent [-h] [--param NAME=VALUE] [--url URL]
                                    [--backend {web,windows,macos,linux,rdp,citrix}]
                                    [--config CONFIG] [--verify VERIFY] [--expect FIELD=VALUE]
                                    [--on-screen TEXT] [--allow-origin URL] [--allow-text TEXT]
                                    [--write-adapter MODULE:ATTR]
                                    [--teach-authorization STATEMENT]
                                    [--approver-root APPROVER_ROOT] [--agent AGENT]
                                    [--vision {code,selective,every_turn}] [--model MODEL]
                                    [--effort EFFORT] [--max-cost MAX_COST] [--task-id TASK_ID]
                                    [--cache CACHE] [--key-dir KEY_DIR] [--policy POLICY]
                                    [--drop-field DROP_FIELD] [--admit-key ADMIT_KEY]
                                    [--admission-policy ADMISSION_POLICY]
                                    [--canary-param NAME=VALUE] [--admit-as ADMIT_AS]
                                    [--hold | --no-hold] [--show-browser] [--json]
                                    prompt [task_dir]

``openadapt-flow compile-agent``: compile an agent's first verified run.

A computer-use agent does the task once in the app at ``--url``. That run is
real: the agent makes the entry in that app. Point ``--url`` at a test copy
with test records. If the system of record shows exactly the record the task
named, the run is compiled into a program that later runs with no model calls.

::

    openadapt-flow compile-agent "Open the referral for Jane Sample and save this note: {note}" \
        --url http://localhost:8080/#tasks --verify verify.yaml \
        --param note="Follow up in two weeks" \
        --expect patient_id=p1 --on-screen "Jane Sample" --on-screen "MRN P1" \
        --admit-key agent.pem --admission-policy signed-policy.json

    openadapt-flow compile-agent run <task dir> --param note="Recheck in ten days"

    openadapt-flow compile-agent admit <task dir> --admit-as "Dana Reviewer" \
        --canary-param note="Canary test note"

``admit`` is for a draft that waits for a person, such as one an agent taught
over MCP (``openadapt-agent serve --teach``): at an interactive terminal the
person confirms the proposed record checks if nobody has yet, reviews the
steps, attends the canary and admits. ``--admit-key`` admits with a
registered key instead, after the checks are confirmed.

The command is re-entrant. Run it again with the same arguments and it picks
up where it stopped: the agent runs only when the task has no draft and no
admitted program. Confirming the proposed record checks is a person's step at
an interactive terminal; without one, the command stops with the draft
waiting and says so.

positional arguments:
  prompt                the task, with {name} for each --param; "run" to run a compiled task;
                        "admit" to confirm and admit a waiting draft; or "emit" / "re-emit" to re-
                        emit mcp/server.py and skills for an admitted task
  task_dir              with run, admit, emit, or re-emit: the compiled task directory

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --param NAME=VALUE
  --url URL             the app's entry URL; the agent makes real entries there, so use a test
                        copy
  --backend {web,windows,macos,linux,rdp,citrix}
                        the surface the app runs on, as for record --backend. A desktop, RDP or
                        Citrix app is named by --config instead
  --config CONFIG       deployment.yaml; a non-web backend section (windows, macos, linux, rdp,
                        citrix) is the app the agent drives, built by build_backend
  --verify VERIFY       verify.yaml whose verifier: section reads the system of record
  --expect FIELD=VALUE  a field the new record must have, such as patient_id=p1
  --on-screen TEXT      the record's identity as the screen shows it; checked before every save
  --allow-origin URL    another origin run 1's browser may reach (a sign-in host, a CDN); every
                        origin but the app's is refused otherwise
  --allow-text TEXT     more text the agent may type in run 1 (a test user name); it may always
                        type the inputs, the --expect values and the --on-screen text
  --write-adapter MODULE:ATTR
                        the app's write adapter (openadapt_flow.teach_scope.WriteAdapter): run 1's
                        writes are read before they are sent
  --teach-authorization STATEMENT
                        a person's signed teach authorization (openadapt-flow teach-
                        authorization): run 1 is scoped by it, and the flags may only narrow it.
                        Without one the draft is refused at admission
  --approver-root APPROVER_ROOT
                        the approver root the teach authorization's signer is checked under
                        (default OPENADAPT_APPROVER_ROOT)
  --agent AGENT         claude (default), or a JSON file of scripted steps or code-action scripts
                        (no model calls)
  --vision {code,selective,every_turn}
                        code (default): act through one terminal-style tool, every save read back
                        (docs/CODE_AS_ACTION.md); selective: the structural listing; every_turn: a
                        screenshot after every action
  --model MODEL         model id (default claude-sonnet-5-5 for code, claude-opus-5-5 otherwise)
  --effort EFFORT
  --max-cost MAX_COST   USD cap for run 1
  --task-id TASK_ID
  --cache CACHE

usage: openadapt-flow console [-h] [--bundles BUNDLES] [--runs RUNS] [--skills SKILLS]
                              [--port PORT] [--allow-actions] [--repair-store REPAIR_STORE]
                              [--attend] [--url URL] [--headed] [--local-grounding]
                              [--allow-model-grounding] [--remote-decisions]
                              [--remote-decision-host URL]
                              [--backend {web,windows,macos,linux,rdp,citrix}] [--agent-url URL]
                              [--macos-app APP] [--macos-window-title TITLE] [--linux-app APP]
                              [--linux-window-title TITLE] [--linux-allow-physical-input]
                              [--rdp-host HOST] [--rdp-window OWNER] [--rdp-window-title TITLE]
                              [--rdp-readiness-text TEXT] [--allow-surface-override]
                              [--invocation-challenge INVOCATION_CHALLENGE] [--config-sha256 HEX]
                              [--config YAML]
                              [--effects-kind {none,rest,fhir,sql,file,document-hash}]
                              [--effects-base-url EFFECTS_BASE_URL]
                              [--effects-records-path EFFECTS_RECORDS_PATH]
                              [--effects-root EFFECTS_ROOT] [--api-actuator]
                              [--api-base-url API_BASE_URL] [--durable]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --bundles BUNDLES     Directory scanned (2 levels deep) for workflow bundle directories
                        (default: current directory)
  --runs RUNS           Directory scanned for run directories (default: runs/)
  --skills SKILLS       Extra directory scanned for skill libraries (skills.json); the bundles
                        directory is always scanned too
  --port PORT           Port on 127.0.0.1 (the bind address is loopback-only, always)
  --allow-actions       Enable executing governed actions (approve / resume / certify / promote /
                        rollback) from the UI after an explicit confirm that shows the exact
                        command. Default: read-only — the UI renders the command for the operator
                        to copy instead
  --repair-store REPAIR_STORE
                        Repair store whose automatic repairs (standard changes) the console lists
                        and, when attended, lets a person revert
  --attend              Open the authenticated local Needs Attention queue first. It is read-only
                        unless --allow-actions is also supplied; attended mutations additionally
                        require an engine-issued pause capability and qualified deployment service
  --url URL             Live browser URL for attended verification/continuation. Required for
                        --backend web unless backend.url is set in --config.
  --headed              Keep the attended browser visible for the operator. The web attended-
                        action path requires a headed session.
  --local-grounding     Pixel surfaces (Citrix, RDP, VNC): find icons and unlabeled controls again
                        after a display-scale, zoom, font or theme change with a local model.
                        Look-alikes halt the step. In process, no outbound calls; the pinned 24 MB
                        weights are fetched once.
  --allow-model-grounding
                        EGRESS OPT-IN: permit configured off-box model components during fresh
                        attended verification and deterministic continuation
  --remote-decisions    Publish open attended pauses to the hosted decision surface over an
                        OUTBOUND-ONLY connection, so a paired phone can answer them from anywhere
                        without any inbound port, certificate, or reverse proxy. Requires --attend
                        --allow-actions, a --config whose human_decisions.remote is enabled with
                        an exact tenant and runner, and OPENADAPT_RUNNER_TOKEN. Only the PHI-free
                        signed task and the closed halt context cross the wire; screenshots never
                        leave
  --remote-decision-host URL
                        Hosted control-plane origin for --remote-decisions (default: the
                        configured hosted host, https://app.openadapt.ai)
  --backend {web,windows,macos,linux,rdp,citrix}
                        Backend to drive: 'web' (Playwright/Chromium), 'windows' (native Windows
                        via the WAA HTTP agent at replay), 'macos' (one native Mac app window),
                        'linux' (one exact AT-SPI app window at replay), 'rdp' (pixel-only network
                        or local remote desktop), or 'citrix' (the local Citrix Workspace window;
                        its owner defaults by host OS and a configured rdp_window may override
                        it). Overrides backend.kind from --config. Omit on record to capture on
                        this OS, or pass --url to record the browser.
  --agent-url URL       Base URL of the in-guest Windows (WAA) agent for --backend windows (e.g.
                        http://localhost:5001). Replay/run only: desktop record refuses this flag
                        because local Capture cannot bind to a WAA endpoint. Overrides
                        backend.agent_url.
  --macos-app APP       Owner application for --backend macos (e.g. MyApp). During record this
                        scopes Capture to that local app window; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.macos_app.
  --macos-window-title TITLE
                        Window-title substring for --backend macos. Ambiguous matches are refused.
                        During record this scopes Capture; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.macos_window_title.
  --linux-app APP       Exact AT-SPI application name for --backend linux (e.g. gedit). Replay/run
                        only: the current Capture path records the local Linux desktop and refuses
                        this flag. Overrides backend.linux_app.
  --linux-window-title TITLE
                        Exact top-level window title for --backend linux. Zero or multiple matches
                        are refused. Replay/run only: the current Capture path records the local
                        Linux desktop and refuses this flag. Overrides backend.linux_window_title.
  --linux-allow-physical-input
                        Explicitly allow window-bound X11 pointer/keyboard fallback for --backend
                        linux replay/run when native AT-SPI actuation is unavailable. Record
                        refuses this replay-only flag.
  --rdp-host HOST       RDP host/IP for --backend rdp (network RDP via FreeRDP). Overrides
                        backend.rdp_host. Replay/run only: record cannot connect local Capture to
                        this endpoint. Record inside the remote session, or capture a local client
                        with --window/--rdp-window.
  --rdp-window OWNER    Exact local remote-display window owner/process for --backend rdp or
                        citrix. On Windows this is the process basename (for example wfica32); on
                        macOS it is the app owner (for example 'Citrix Viewer'). During record it
                        also scopes local Capture to that window; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.rdp_window.
  --rdp-window-title TITLE
                        Exact local remote-display window title used to disambiguate multiple
                        matching RDP/Citrix client windows. During record it also scopes local
                        Capture; during replay/run it overrides backend.rdp_window_title.
  --rdp-readiness-text TEXT
                        Stable text that must be visible in the current remote frame before input.
                        Required for governed Citrix `run`; overrides backend.rdp_readiness_text.
  --allow-surface-override
                        Explicitly permit executing a workflow on a DIFFERENT surface than the one
                        it was recorded/qualified on (Workflow.surface). Off by default: a cross-
                        surface run is refused. The override is recorded in the run report
                        (surface_override) as compatibility evidence; it is never silent.
  --invocation-challenge INVOCATION_CHALLENGE
                        Non-authority freshness challenge for the local Standard producer.
  --config-sha256 HEX   The SHA-256 of --config's bytes. Flow opens the file once (not through a
                        symlink; it must be a regular file), refuses it if the digest differs, and
                        from then on parses only those bytes whenever this command loads that
                        path, so replacing the file, or a symlink put in its place, changes
                        nothing
  --config YAML         Deployment config YAML wiring backend / actuation / effects / runtime /
                        policy (see docs/deployment.example.yaml). Direct flags below override
                        individual fields.
  --effects-kind {none,rest,fhir,sql,file,document-hash}
                        System-of-record EffectVerifier to wire so consequential writes are
                        verified against the real record (not the screen). rest needs --effects-
                        records-path; the fhir/sql/file kinds need their config fields
                        (resource_type and field_paths, sql_query, root, ...) from a --config
                        deployment YAML
  --effects-base-url EFFECTS_BASE_URL
                        Base URL for the rest / fhir effect verifier
  --effects-records-path EFFECTS_RECORDS_PATH
                        Path whose GET returns the app's records (rest effect verifier)
  --effects-root EFFECTS_ROOT
                        Document-store root for the document-hash effect verifier
  --api-actuator        Wire the API/tool actuation tier: a step carrying an ApiBinding is
                        performed via the API (deterministic, $0) and confirmed by the effect
                        verifier, skipping the GUI
  --api-base-url API_BASE_URL
                        Base URL for the API actuator (implies --api-actuator)
  --durable             Enable the Tier-3 durable runtime: checkpoint each verified step and
                        durably PAUSE on halt, so the run is resumable via `resume` (never re-
                        performing a confirmed write)

Also available as: openadapt-flow services console

help.openadapt-flow flight:
usage: openadapt-flow flight [-h] [--task-id TASK_ID] [--out OUT] [--label LABEL]
                             [--gate {terminal,file,refuse}] [--approval-timeout APPROVAL_TIMEOUT]
                             [--cdp CDP] [--guard-config GUARD_CONFIG] [--guard-task GUARD_TASK]
                             [--max-cost-usd MAX_COST_USD] [--no-scrub] [--i-accept-unscrubbed]
                             [--safe-label LABEL] [--allow-unenforced-egress] [--no-egress-block]
                             [--json]
                             ...

``openadapt-flow flight``: record any agent's run, gate its commits.

    openadapt-flow flight [--task-id ID] [--cdp URL] [--max-cost-usd N] -- CMD ...

Starts a loopback proxy in front of the model API and runs CMD with
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and OPENAI_BASE_URL pointing at it, so every model call
is metered and priced, and the request's text and its screenshots in PNG,
JPEG, GIF, BMP, TIFF or WEBP are scrubbed of personal data on this machine
before it is sent (other image formats, and data an agent re-encodes on
purpose, are not covered; see "What the scrubber does not cover" in
FLIGHT_RECORDER.md). The provider the agent
already targets (its own *_BASE_URL, else the provider's API) is the only
place anything is sent; the agent's key passes through untouched and is
never logged.

CMD also gets OPENADAPT_FLIGHT_GATE_URL: an executor wrapped with
GatedComputer or GatedComputerCall (one line, see FLIGHT_RECORDER.md) logs
its actions here and holds each click that is not known to be safe (only
focus/view roles and a short list such as Cancel, Close, Back, Search, Open
pass; --safe-label adds to it) for a person: --gate terminal asks y/N on
this terminal, --gate file writes an item-approval request Desktop or a
paired phone answers, --gate refuse holds every one.

CMD runs under an OS egress block (openadapt_flow.flight.egress): on macOS,
sandbox-exec denies every outbound connection except to loopback, so a
direct connection from CMD or anything it starts (a browser included)
fails; work handed to a process outside that tree is not covered. Where the block isn't available
(any other system) the run refuses to start unless --allow-unenforced-egress
is given; --no-egress-block turns it off on macOS too. Either is recorded in
flight.json and egress.json.

The run is marked refused (exit 3, flight.json details.egress.refused) when
model calls went around the proxy: CMD's usage.json (OPENADAPT_USAGE_PATH,
openadapt.agent-usage/v1) reports more calls than the proxy saw, or a direct
connection through the proxy variables was trapped.

With --cdp (or when CMD starts Chromium with --remote-debugging-port), the
existing `openadapt-flow guard` also attaches to the browser, given
--guard-config and --guard-task.

Writes flight.json (openadapt.flight-run/v1), egress.json, timeline.jsonl,
scrubbed frame thumbnails and timeline.html in the run directory, and prints
its path. Exit status: CMD's own; 3 when the run is refused for egress
outside the proxy; 2 when the run could not start (no scrubber, no egress
block, a bad option, CMD not found).

positional arguments:
  command               -- CMD ...

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --task-id TASK_ID     the task this run does (default: generated)
  --out OUT             the run directory (default: flight-runs/<time>-<task>)
  --label LABEL         names the agent or worker in flight.json (default: CMD's name)
  --gate {terminal,file,refuse}
                        who decides a held action: y/N on this terminal (refuses with no
                        terminal), an item-approval request for Desktop or a phone, or nobody
  --approval-timeout APPROVAL_TIMEOUT
                        seconds --gate file waits for a person before the action stays held
  --cdp CDP             the agent's Chromium DevTools URL, to run the guard
  --guard-config GUARD_CONFIG
                        guard.yaml for the guard
  --guard-task GUARD_TASK
                        the guard's task file (openadapt.guard-task/v1)
  --max-cost-usd MAX_COST_USD
                        refuse model calls (HTTP 429) once this much is spent; an unpriced model
                        is refused too, since the cap can't be enforced
  --no-scrub            send screenshots and text unscrubbed (needs --i-accept-unscrubbed)
  --i-accept-unscrubbed
                        confirm --no-scrub; recorded in flight.json and the local ledger
  --safe-label LABEL    a control label a click may pass on without a person, besides the built-in
                        Cancel, Close, Back, Search, Open, View... (repeatable; a label with Save,
                        Submit, Send... is refused); recorded in flight.json
  --allow-unenforced-egress
                        run even where the OS egress block is not available (any system but
                        macOS); a call that skips the proxy is then not blocked. Recorded
  --no-egress-block     don't put CMD under the OS egress block even where it is available (the
                        behaviour before the block); recorded
  --json                print flight.json

Also available as: openadapt-flow run --flight

usage: openadapt-flow guard [-h] --cdp CDP --config CONFIG --task TASK --out OUT
                            [--page-url PAGE_URL] [--observe-only]
                            [--approval {not_gated,each_item}] [--timeout TIMEOUT]
                            [--attach-wait ATTACH_WAIT] [--secret FIELD] [--no-teach]
                            [--ledger-row | --no-ledger-row] [--json]

``openadapt-flow guard``: guard an agent you already run.

Start your agent's Chromium with a DevTools port (the one line you add), then
start the guard for the task before the agent starts it::

    openadapt-flow guard --cdp http://127.0.0.1:9222 \
        --config guard.yaml --task task.json --out runs/task-0001

The guard attaches to the agent's tab, holds every save until the record on
screen is the one ``task.json`` names, reads the save back, and records the
run. With a ``teach:`` section, a run that reads back correctly becomes a
draft program a person confirms and admits (``compile-agent admit``).

Exit status: 0 the save was read back VERIFIED; 3 a save was blocked and none
went through; 4 the save went through and was not verified (REFUTED or
RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED: a person checks the record); 5 no save was seen;
2 the config, the task or the browser could not be used.

options:

                        (http://127.0.0.1:9222)

  --approval {not_gated,each_item}

usage: openadapt-flow hooks [-h] {install,status,uninstall,approve,run} ...

``openadapt hooks``: check a coding agent's writes to declared systems.

    openadapt hooks install --agent claude-code     # or codex
    openadapt hooks status
    openadapt hooks approve ap-1a2b3c4d5e6f         # a held call or write
    openadapt hooks uninstall

``install`` writes project-local hook settings only (never your global
``~/.claude`` or ``~/.codex``). Each tool call that writes to a system
declared in ``openadapt.systems.yaml`` is pre-checked, read back and given
a signed receipt. Hooks see tool calls, so they are advisory against an agent
that has its own credentials and shell. See ``docs/HOOKS.md``.

usage: openadapt-flow induce [-h] --out OUT [--name NAME] [--held-out] [--probe-on DEPLOYMENT]
                             [--probe-work-dir PROBE_WORK_DIR] [--report REPORT]
                             [--accept-narrated LOCATION@GUARD_ID] [--accepted-by ACCEPTED_BY]
                             [--narration-model]

positional arguments:

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --out OUT             Output program-bundle directory (written only when CERTIFIED)
  --name NAME           Name for the induced workflow (default: 'induced-program')
  --held-out            Also print the leave-one-out STRUCTURAL held-out coverage (needs >= 2
                        traces). It compares program shape with each held-out trace, executes
                        nothing and checks neither identity nor effects; for a generalization
                        claim run held-out items with
                        openadapt_flow.validation.behavioral_generalization
  --probe-on DEPLOYMENT
                        Settle refused optional steps by replaying each reading (step dropped /
                        step kept when present) in a fresh session on the test copy this
                        deployment file declares (test_copy.declared: true), scored by its reward
                        contract's read-back. Refuses any target not declared a test copy. See
                        docs/PROBE_INDUCTION.md

                        directory, removed afterwards)

help.openadapt-flow plan:
usage: openadapt-flow plan [-h] {create,show,apply,undo,release,cancel,approve,status} ...

``openadapt plan``: dry-run, apply and undo a batch of writes to external systems.

    openadapt plan create --tx openadapt.tx.yaml --task T-1 writes.json
    openadapt plan show PLAN
    openadapt plan approve PLAN           # a person, at a terminal
    openadapt plan apply PLAN
    openadapt plan undo PLAN
    openadapt plan release PLAN           # irreversible writes after holdback
    openadapt plan cancel PLAN            # drop held writes before release
    openadapt plan status

``create`` reads every record the batch touches, predicts the diff (a staged
transaction for a database, a computed shadow for a REST API, the holdback
queue for email) and prints what would change. ``approve`` binds to that exact
plan digest, once. ``apply`` refuses a plan whose records moved since, and
each write carries an idempotency key derived from the task and the record,
never from the payload: a retried or regenerated write with a different
payload is refused. ``undo`` compensates each write and proves it by reading
every record and the whole frame back. See ``docs/TRANSACTIONS.md``.

positional arguments:
  {create,show,apply,undo,release,cancel,approve,status}
    create              read the baseline and print the predicted diff
    show                print a plan
    apply               apply an approved plan
    undo                undo an applied plan and prove it by read-back
    release             release held irreversible writes whose holdback passed
    cancel              cancel held writes before release
    approve             approve one plan digest, once (a person at a terminal)
    status              list held writes and ledger entries

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

Also available as: openadapt-flow run --plan

help.openadapt-flow qualify:
Qualify: before a compiled workflow may run unattended on a real system, run it against the normal case and deliberate faults, and confirm it is verified by reading back the system of record and halts on every fault.

usage: openadapt-flow qualify <bundle> --verify verify.yaml [--cases ...] [--out DIR] [--certify [POLICY]] [--run-params FILE]
       openadapt-flow qualify <command> ...

The faults are a duplicated save button, a relabeled save button, a blanked
screen, and a weak or missing check that the write happened. Certifying
(--certify) signs the result under a policy such as clinical-write; you get a
signed report and a certified bundle the runner will admit. A certificate
covers only the environment the workflow was qualified in.

Definitions of qualify and certify:
  https://docs.openadapt.ai/reference/glossary/#qualify
Certification policies (built-in clinical-write and permissive, or your own
YAML file passed to --certify):
  https://docs.openadapt.ai/reference/glossary/#certification-policy
How to write verify.yaml:
  https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/QUALIFY_A_WORKFLOW.md

positional arguments:
  {campaign,schema,label,init,propose,accept,admit-local,from-demo,inspect,explain,report,set-identity,set-risk,trust-runner,set-effect,business-decision,judgment-cases,add-case,run,run-case,drills,add-requalification,certify}
    campaign            Qualify a bundle from verify.yaml (also the default form: `qualify
                        <bundle> --verify verify.yaml`)
    schema              Print the qualification-project JSON Schema
    label               Optionally set, remove, or list presentation-only entity labels
    init                Initialize a bundle's qualification project
    propose             Draft application, environment, identity, and effect pins from the
                        compiled demo. Missing pins HALT; nothing is guessed. Runs the proposed
                        oracle against a --break-it fault.
    accept              Confirm every proposed pin in one command after the proposed oracle
                        catches a --break-it fault. Refusing a pin HALTs.
    admit-local         Sign a local-dev admission for an accepted proposal. The signer cannot
                        enter a production trust map.
    from-demo           Propose pins from the demo, accept them, and optionally sign a local-dev
                        admission. After record and compile.
    inspect             Inspect qualification coverage
    explain             Explain qualification coverage
    report              Report qualification coverage
    set-identity        Set exact/normalized identity fields and their quorum
    set-risk            Confirm an action's reviewed business-risk classification
    trust-runner        Trust an Ed25519 qualification-runner public key
    set-effect          Assign verification-strength tier to an existing effect
    business-decision   Add, update, or inspect one reviewed finite business decision without
                        editing the workflow manifest
    judgment-cases      Store or check reviewed local judgment cases; this command never
                        synthesizes an executable rule from examples
    add-case            Add a representative or fault case
    run                 Import case results produced by the Desktop/local/customer-controlled
                        qualification runner
    run-case            Run one current qualification case (the practice item or a readiness
                        drill) with Flow-owned Standard authorization
    drills              Add the five readiness drills for the practice case's save and trust this
                        computer's local drill key (a local campaign)
    add-requalification
                        Add a condition that requires this workflow to be requalified
    certify             Persist a combined qualification and existing-policy decision

positional arguments:

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --case-id CASE_ID     Declared practice case or readiness drill
  --inputs JSON         Private canonical runtime-input artifact from Desktop (mode 0600; params
                        and worklists only)
  --campaign-id CAMPAIGN_ID
                        Local campaign identity
  --run-id RUN_ID       One local case-attempt identity
  --qualification-campaign-authority-file PATH
                        Private owner-only signed non-production authority for this exact trial;
                        required once the run actuates under a campaign permit
  --run-dir RUN_DIR     New durable case-attempt directory
  --url URL             Target app URL
  --headed              Run browser headed
  --dry-run             Validate without input
  --fault-driver NAME   A drill's fault driver from the openadapt_flow.qualification_fault_drivers
                        entry point (a configured campaign). Without it, a drill uses this
                        computer's local drill campaign (see `qualify drills`).
  --backend {web,windows,macos,linux,rdp,citrix}
                        Backend to drive: 'web' (Playwright/Chromium), 'windows' (native Windows
                        via the WAA HTTP agent at replay), 'macos' (one native Mac app window),
                        'linux' (one exact AT-SPI app window at replay), 'rdp' (pixel-only network
                        or local remote desktop), or 'citrix' (the local Citrix Workspace window;
                        its owner defaults by host OS and a configured rdp_window may override
                        it). Overrides backend.kind from --config. Omit on record to capture on
                        this OS, or pass --url to record the browser.
  --agent-url URL       Base URL of the in-guest Windows (WAA) agent for --backend windows (e.g.
                        http://localhost:5001). Replay/run only: desktop record refuses this flag
                        because local Capture cannot bind to a WAA endpoint. Overrides
                        backend.agent_url.
  --macos-app APP       Owner application for --backend macos (e.g. MyApp). During record this
                        scopes Capture to that local app window; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.macos_app.
  --macos-window-title TITLE
                        Window-title substring for --backend macos. Ambiguous matches are refused.
                        During record this scopes Capture; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.macos_window_title.
  --linux-app APP       Exact AT-SPI application name for --backend linux (e.g. gedit). Replay/run
                        only: the current Capture path records the local Linux desktop and refuses
                        this flag. Overrides backend.linux_app.
  --linux-window-title TITLE
                        Exact top-level window title for --backend linux. Zero or multiple matches
                        are refused. Replay/run only: the current Capture path records the local
                        Linux desktop and refuses this flag. Overrides backend.linux_window_title.
  --linux-allow-physical-input
                        Explicitly allow window-bound X11 pointer/keyboard fallback for --backend
                        linux replay/run when native AT-SPI actuation is unavailable. Record
                        refuses this replay-only flag.
  --rdp-host HOST       RDP host/IP for --backend rdp (network RDP via FreeRDP). Overrides
                        backend.rdp_host. Replay/run only: record cannot connect local Capture to
                        this endpoint. Record inside the remote session, or capture a local client
                        with --window/--rdp-window.
  --rdp-window OWNER    Exact local remote-display window owner/process for --backend rdp or
                        citrix. On Windows this is the process basename (for example wfica32); on
                        macOS it is the app owner (for example 'Citrix Viewer'). During record it
                        also scopes local Capture to that window; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.rdp_window.
  --rdp-window-title TITLE
                        Exact local remote-display window title used to disambiguate multiple
                        matching RDP/Citrix client windows. During record it also scopes local
                        Capture; during replay/run it overrides backend.rdp_window_title.
  --rdp-readiness-text TEXT
                        Stable text that must be visible in the current remote frame before input.
                        Required for governed Citrix `run`; overrides backend.rdp_readiness_text.
  --allow-surface-override
                        Explicitly permit executing a workflow on a DIFFERENT surface than the one
                        it was recorded/qualified on (Workflow.surface). Off by default: a cross-
                        surface run is refused. The override is recorded in the run report
                        (surface_override) as compatibility evidence; it is never silent.
  --browser-cdp-endpoint URL
                        Run in an already-running, signed-in local Chromium through its loopback
                        DevTools endpoint (for example, http://127.0.0.1:9222) instead of
                        launching a new, signed-out browser. The run binds the one open tab on the
                        --url origin, starts from the screen it shows, and never navigates or
                        closes the browser. Overrides backend.browser_cdp_endpoint from --config.
  --browser-page-url URL
                        Exact current URL of the tab to run in, when more than one open tab has
                        the --url origin. Requires --browser-cdp-endpoint.
  --invocation-challenge INVOCATION_CHALLENGE
                        Non-authority freshness challenge for the local Standard producer.
  --config-sha256 HEX   The SHA-256 of --config's bytes. Flow opens the file once (not through a
                        symlink; it must be a regular file), refuses it if the digest differs, and
                        from then on parses only those bytes whenever this command loads that
                        path, so replacing the file, or a symlink put in its place, changes
                        nothing
  --config YAML         Deployment config YAML wiring backend / actuation / effects / runtime /
                        policy (see docs/deployment.example.yaml). Direct flags below override
                        individual fields.
  --effects-kind {none,rest,fhir,sql,file,document-hash}
                        System-of-record EffectVerifier to wire so consequential writes are
                        verified against the real record (not the screen). rest needs --effects-
                        records-path; the fhir/sql/file kinds need their config fields
                        (resource_type and field_paths, sql_query, root, ...) from a --config
                        deployment YAML
  --effects-base-url EFFECTS_BASE_URL
                        Base URL for the rest / fhir effect verifier
  --effects-records-path EFFECTS_RECORDS_PATH
                        Path whose GET returns the app's records (rest effect verifier)
  --effects-root EFFECTS_ROOT
                        Document-store root for the document-hash effect verifier
  --api-actuator        Wire the API/tool actuation tier: a step carrying an ApiBinding is
                        performed via the API (deterministic, $0) and confirmed by the effect
                        verifier, skipping the GUI
  --api-base-url API_BASE_URL
                        Base URL for the API actuator (implies --api-actuator)
  --durable             Enable the Tier-3 durable runtime: checkpoint each verified step and
                        durably PAUSE on halt, so the run is resumable via `resume` (never re-
                        performing a confirmed write)
  --approver-root HEX   The root approver key (64 hex) this run trusts: a person's answer counts
                        only when its signer is on the signed approver roster this key vouches
                        for. Also set by the deployment config's approvers.root_public_key or
                        OPENADAPT_APPROVER_ROOT; without one, a person's answer is refused
  --key-dir KEY_DIR     Key directory with the signed approver roster (approvers.json) that
                        approvals are checked against; use the one you approved with (default
                        $OPENADAPT_JIT_KEY_DIR or ~/.openadapt/jit)
  --approver-policy FILE
                        A person-signed approver grant (openadapt-flow approver-grant sign): which
                        agents or systems may answer which classes of save, until when. Without a
                        grant that verifies against the signer registry, only a person may answer;
                        an unsigned or tampered file gives no authority. A clinical_write save
                        takes a non-person approver only when the grant's policy pins an opt-in.
  --started-by ID       The agent or system that started this run (opaque id). It can never answer
                        this run's saves. openadapt-agent sets it.
  --approver-webhook URL
                        Ask this https endpoint (the customer's approver agent or system) about
                        each waiting save, with HMAC-signed, PHI-free messages. The secret is read
                        from OPENADAPT_APPROVER_WEBHOOK_SECRET. A person can still answer in
                        Desktop. Needs --approver-webhook-id and a policy that allows the
                        approver's kind.
  --approver-webhook-id APPROVER_WEBHOOK_ID
                        The webhook approver's opaque id, such as system:acme-approvals
  --approver-webhook-kind {agent,system}
                        Whether the webhook approver is an agent or a system (default system)
  --approval-mode {each_item,problems_only,not_gated}
                        Per-item approval before each consequential save. each_item (the default
                        for every run): the run waits before every save until a person approves it
                        in Desktop's Run it (see `item-approval`). problems_only: only problems go
                        to a person; until a switch record is configured, every save still asks.
                        not_gated: no per-item pause, recorded in the report (the hosted runner,
                        Execute and MCP callers). Overrides runtime.approval_mode. A resume always
                        keeps the run's own mode.
  --approval-wait SECONDS
                        How long the run waits for a person's answer before it stops before the
                        save (default 900, at most 14400). An answer given later can still be used
                        by `resume`.
  --subroutine-library JSON
                        Current subroutine library to re-admit embedded subroutines against before
                        this run. Required when the bundle embeds a subroutine; a certification
                        made before a newer version was published does not let the old version
                        run.
  --subroutine-workflow-id ID
                        Id this workflow was registered under when it was certified (default: the
                        workflow name)

usage: openadapt-flow record [-h] [--url URL] [--browser-cdp-endpoint URL]
                             [--browser-page-url URL] --out OUT [--secret FIELD] [--param FIELD]
                             [--identifier FIELD|X,Y,W,H] [--task TASK] [--until-cmd CMD]
                             [--window OWNER] [--window-title SUBSTRING] [--headless]
                             [--profile {demo,standard,regulated}] [--no-encrypt]
                             [--capture-network] [--with-check] [--verify [VERIFY_YAML]]
                             [--surface NAME=KIND:WINDOW] [--yes]
                             [--backend {web,windows,macos,linux,rdp,citrix}] [--agent-url URL]
                             [--macos-app APP] [--macos-window-title TITLE] [--linux-app APP]
                             [--linux-window-title TITLE] [--linux-allow-physical-input]
                             [--rdp-host HOST] [--rdp-window OWNER] [--rdp-window-title TITLE]
                             [--rdp-readiness-text TEXT] [--allow-surface-override]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --url URL             URL of the app to record against (required for --backend web)
  --browser-cdp-endpoint URL
                        Attach the web recorder to an already-running local Chromium browser
                        through its loopback DevTools endpoint (for example,
                        http://127.0.0.1:9222). The recorder selects a tab on the --url origin and
                        does not launch, navigate, or close the browser.
  --browser-page-url URL
                        Exact current URL of the existing tab to record. Use this with --browser-
                        cdp-endpoint when more than one open tab has the --url origin.
  --out OUT             Recording output directory
  --secret FIELD        Mark a typed field (by name or id) as a SECRET; its value is never
                        persisted and is injected at replay from OPENADAPT_FLOW_SECRET_<FIELD>.
                        input[type=password] is always treated as secret. Repeatable.
  --param FIELD         Record a typed value as a PARAMETER; its demonstrated value becomes the
                        default, overridable at replay with --param. For --backend web, FIELD is
                        the field name/id. For --backend windows/macos/linux/rdp/citrix (capture
                        has no field identity), use NAME=VALUE — the typed value equal to VALUE is
                        marked as parameter NAME. Repeatable.
  --identifier FIELD|X,Y,W,H
                        Mark the RECORD-IDENTIFYING region (patient banner / MRN field) so the
                        compiler crops its pixels (anchor.identifier_crop) and the pixel-compare
                        identity tier arms on remote-display/pixel replays (Citrix/RDP). For
                        --backend web, FIELD is the field name/id (repeatable; the first marked
                        field present at each click contributes its rect). For --backend
                        windows/macos/linux/rdp/citrix (a pixel capture has no field identity),
                        give the region once as X,Y,W,H in recording pixels. Unmarked recordings
                        still get automatic crops on identity-armed pixel steps (from the OCR
                        identity band).
  --task TASK           Task description for a desktop (--backend windows/macos/linux/rdp/citrix)
                        capture session (stored in the recording metadata).
  --until-cmd CMD       Run CMD on an interval while recording. Exit 0 stops the record. The
                        command is not captured as clicks. Ctrl-C still stops. A non-zero exit
                        keeps recording (probe failure is not done).
  --window OWNER        Scope a desktop capture (--backend windows/macos/linux/rdp/citrix) to ONE
                        window, recorded in that window's OWN pixel space (owner-app substring,
                        e.g. --window Parallels / --window 'Citrix Workspace'). Closes the
                        coordinate-space gap with the pixel (rdp) replay surface. Combine with
                        --window-title to disambiguate. Supported on macOS and Windows hosts;
                        refused elsewhere. Ignored (rejected) for --backend web.
  --window-title SUBSTRING
                        Title substring to disambiguate the --window target when the owner app has
                        multiple windows (case-insensitive; may be used with or without --window).
                        The resolved title is stored in the LOCAL recording metadata only.
  --headless            Run the browser headless (scripted/CI recording)
  --profile {demo,standard,regulated}
                        Recording posture (Section 5). standard/regulated REQUIRE an explicit
                        --backend (no implicit browser default in production). demo may omit
                        --backend: it defaults to capture on this OS (macos/windows/linux), or to
                        the browser when --url is given, and prints a visible notice. Omitted: the
                        same permissive pre-profile default.
  --no-encrypt          Write a web recording in plaintext (recorded in ~/.openadapt/plaintext-at-
                        rest.jsonl). Web recordings are encrypted by default, under the configured
                        key or a local one; refused under OPENADAPT_FLOW_AT_REST=strict
  --capture-network     Web only: also keep the page's requests (network.jsonl; cookies, passwords
                        and session tokens withheld). compile then proposes an API step for a save
                        it can repeat as one request; a person admits it with 'api admit'
  --with-check          After the save, also show how you'd check it saved (reload or search
                        again, open the record). Flow then asks which fields show the values you
                        typed and writes check.json
  --verify [VERIFY_YAML]
                        Read the system of record through the verifier: section of this file
                        (rest, sql, fhir, graphql or file) before and after the recording, and
                        propose the checks for what changed in verify.proposed.yaml. Both reads go
                        to sor_snapshots.json (mode 0600). With no file, look the record up after
                        you save: that look-up becomes the proposed check
  --surface NAME=KIND:WINDOW
                        With no --backend or --url, record follows you across windows on its own.
                        Use --surface to name the windows yourself instead, or --surface auto with
                        --url to add automatic windows to a browser recording. Declare each
                        desktop or remote window the person works in (repeatable). KIND is
                        windows, macos, linux, rdp or citrix; WINDOW is part of that window's
                        title (on macOS, the app name). Repeat a NAME to add another window to it,
                        such as its dialog. With --url the browser leads; otherwise the first
                        --surface does. Each change of window becomes a checked switch step. An
                        action in a window you did not declare stops the recording. See
                        docs/MULTI_SURFACE.md.
  --yes                 Keep a cross-window recording's surfaces without asking. Without a
                        terminal and without --yes, the recording is kept unconfirmed and compile
                        refuses it until confirm-surfaces is run.
  --backend {web,windows,macos,linux,rdp,citrix}
                        Backend to drive: 'web' (Playwright/Chromium), 'windows' (native Windows
                        via the WAA HTTP agent at replay), 'macos' (one native Mac app window),
                        'linux' (one exact AT-SPI app window at replay), 'rdp' (pixel-only network
                        or local remote desktop), or 'citrix' (the local Citrix Workspace window;
                        its owner defaults by host OS and a configured rdp_window may override
                        it). Overrides backend.kind from --config. Omit on record to capture on
                        this OS, or pass --url to record the browser.
  --agent-url URL       Base URL of the in-guest Windows (WAA) agent for --backend windows (e.g.
                        http://localhost:5001). Replay/run only: desktop record refuses this flag
                        because local Capture cannot bind to a WAA endpoint. Overrides
                        backend.agent_url.
  --macos-app APP       Owner application for --backend macos (e.g. MyApp). During record this
                        scopes Capture to that local app window; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.macos_app.
  --macos-window-title TITLE
                        Window-title substring for --backend macos. Ambiguous matches are refused.
                        During record this scopes Capture; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.macos_window_title.
  --linux-app APP       Exact AT-SPI application name for --backend linux (e.g. gedit). Replay/run
                        only: the current Capture path records the local Linux desktop and refuses
                        this flag. Overrides backend.linux_app.
  --linux-window-title TITLE
                        Exact top-level window title for --backend linux. Zero or multiple matches
                        are refused. Replay/run only: the current Capture path records the local
                        Linux desktop and refuses this flag. Overrides backend.linux_window_title.
  --linux-allow-physical-input
                        Explicitly allow window-bound X11 pointer/keyboard fallback for --backend
                        linux replay/run when native AT-SPI actuation is unavailable. Record
                        refuses this replay-only flag.
  --rdp-host HOST       RDP host/IP for --backend rdp (network RDP via FreeRDP). Overrides
                        backend.rdp_host. Replay/run only: record cannot connect local Capture to
                        this endpoint. Record inside the remote session, or capture a local client
                        with --window/--rdp-window.
  --rdp-window OWNER    Exact local remote-display window owner/process for --backend rdp or
                        citrix. On Windows this is the process basename (for example wfica32); on
                        macOS it is the app owner (for example 'Citrix Viewer'). During record it
                        also scopes local Capture to that window; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.rdp_window.
  --rdp-window-title TITLE
                        Exact local remote-display window title used to disambiguate multiple
                        matching RDP/Citrix client windows. During record it also scopes local
                        Capture; during replay/run it overrides backend.rdp_window_title.
  --rdp-readiness-text TEXT
                        Stable text that must be visible in the current remote frame before input.
                        Required for governed Citrix `run`; overrides backend.rdp_readiness_text.
  --allow-surface-override
                        Explicitly permit executing a workflow on a DIFFERENT surface than the one
                        it was recorded/qualified on (Workflow.surface). Off by default: a cross-
                        surface run is refused. The override is recorded in the run report
                        (surface_override) as compatibility evidence; it is never silent.

Related operations (immediately after the task name): confirm-surfaces, narration, sections

help.openadapt-flow repair:
usage: openadapt-flow repair [-h]
                             {register,list,show,review,campaign,approve,stage,canary,canary-record,rollback,status,revert,standard-changes,clear-hold}
                             ...

positional arguments:
  {register,list,show,review,campaign,approve,stage,canary,canary-record,rollback,status,revert,standard-changes,clear-hold}
    register            Register a (prior, proposed) bundle pair as a repair candidate; refuses
                        (fail closed) any contract weakening without a new qualification revision
    list                List candidates and their lifecycle states
    show                Show a candidate's reviewable diff, campaigns, and state
    review              Record a human review of the candidate's diff
    campaign            Run a campaign against the candidate's evidence frames: 'replay' (healthy
                        drift battery must all pass) or 'fault' (ambiguity / wrong-entity / stale-
                        target / dialog / verifier-failure frames must all be REFUSED)
    approve             HUMAN approval gating promotion; refuses unless the diff was reviewed and
                        BOTH campaigns passed. Binds the exact bundle hashes
    stage               Copy BOTH bundles into the store by content hash and re-verify them byte-
                        exact (prior too, so rollback is always local)
    canary              Atomically activate the staged bundle in CANARY mode: a bounded first-N-
                        runs window with per-run verification before full active
    canary-record       Record one canary run from its run directory; any silent-incorrect or
                        verification regression auto-reverts to the prior bundle
    rollback            One-command rollback: restore the prior bundle hash as the active pointer
    status              Show the atomic active-bundle pointer and its lineage
    revert              Undo a repair that applied without a person: the prior bundle is active
                        again, and repairs of that step go to a person
    standard-changes    List the repairs that applied without a person (the daily digest)
    clear-hold          Let repairs of a step apply without a person again after a revert

options:

usage: openadapt-flow replay [-h] [--stop-before-effect] [--url URL] [--demo-app] [--drift DRIFT]
                             [--run-dir RUN_DIR] [--param K=V] [--params-file PARAMS_FILE]
                             [--local-grounding] [--allow-model-grounding]
                             [--save-healed-to SAVE_HEALED_TO] [--headed] [--record-video DIR]
                             [--backend {web,windows,macos,linux,rdp,citrix}] [--agent-url URL]
                             [--macos-app APP] [--macos-window-title TITLE] [--linux-app APP]
                             [--linux-window-title TITLE] [--linux-allow-physical-input]
                             [--rdp-host HOST] [--rdp-window OWNER] [--rdp-window-title TITLE]
                             [--rdp-readiness-text TEXT] [--allow-surface-override]
                             [--surface NAME=KIND[:TARGET]] [--browser-cdp-endpoint URL]
                             [--browser-page-url URL]
                             [--invocation-challenge INVOCATION_CHALLENGE] [--config-sha256 HEX]
                             [--config YAML]
                             [--effects-kind {none,rest,fhir,sql,file,document-hash}]
                             [--effects-base-url EFFECTS_BASE_URL]
                             [--effects-records-path EFFECTS_RECORDS_PATH]
                             [--effects-root EFFECTS_ROOT] [--api-actuator]
                             [--api-base-url API_BASE_URL] [--durable]
                             [--worklist [RELATION=]FILE] [--workers N] [--readback-window K]
                             [--attest-contract PATH] [--attest-sign-key PATH]
                             [--attest-audit-log PATH] [--attest-pre-state PATH] [--no-encrypt]
                             bundle

positional arguments:
  bundle                Workflow bundle directory

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --stop-before-effect  Check it without application input: observe a prefilled screen, then stop
                        before the first input. Unproved prefixes refuse; web requires an
                        attached, already-open page.
  --url URL             URL of the target app
  --demo-app            Serve the bundled demo app and replay against it (for a bundle recorded on
                        it, such as the tutorial's)
  --drift DRIFT         Comma-separated demo drift modes (theme,move,rename,modal) to demonstrate
                        bounded drift resolution; only with --demo-app
  --run-dir RUN_DIR     Run output directory (default: runs/replay-<UTC timestamp> under the
                        current directory)
  --param K=V           Parameter substitution (repeatable)
  --params-file PARAMS_FILE
                        JSON object of parameter bindings; keeps values out of process arguments
                        for managed execution
  --local-grounding     Pixel surfaces (Citrix, RDP, VNC): find icons and unlabeled controls again
                        after a display-scale, zoom, font or theme change with a local model.
                        Look-alikes halt the step. In process, no outbound calls; the pinned 24 MB
                        weights are fetched once.
  --allow-model-grounding
                        EGRESS OPT-IN (PHI audit REM-3): permit wiring an off-box model grounder /
                        identity-VLM / state-verifier (a paid API or an on-prem VLM appliance via
                        OPENADAPT_FLOW_VLM_URL). Screenshots may leave the box. Off by default:
                        replay is fully local with zero outbound calls.
  --save-healed-to SAVE_HEALED_TO
                        Write the healed bundle to this directory
  --headed              Run the browser headed
  --record-video DIR    OPT-IN: capture a WebM video of the replay session into DIR (default: off;
                        no effect on the run directory or report)
  --backend {web,windows,macos,linux,rdp,citrix}
                        Backend to drive: 'web' (Playwright/Chromium), 'windows' (native Windows
                        via the WAA HTTP agent at replay), 'macos' (one native Mac app window),
                        'linux' (one exact AT-SPI app window at replay), 'rdp' (pixel-only network
                        or local remote desktop), or 'citrix' (the local Citrix Workspace window;
                        its owner defaults by host OS and a configured rdp_window may override
                        it). Overrides backend.kind from --config. Omit on record to capture on
                        this OS, or pass --url to record the browser.
  --agent-url URL       Base URL of the in-guest Windows (WAA) agent for --backend windows (e.g.
                        http://localhost:5001). Replay/run only: desktop record refuses this flag
                        because local Capture cannot bind to a WAA endpoint. Overrides
                        backend.agent_url.
  --macos-app APP       Owner application for --backend macos (e.g. MyApp). During record this
                        scopes Capture to that local app window; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.macos_app.
  --macos-window-title TITLE
                        Window-title substring for --backend macos. Ambiguous matches are refused.
                        During record this scopes Capture; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.macos_window_title.
  --linux-app APP       Exact AT-SPI application name for --backend linux (e.g. gedit). Replay/run
                        only: the current Capture path records the local Linux desktop and refuses
                        this flag. Overrides backend.linux_app.
  --linux-window-title TITLE
                        Exact top-level window title for --backend linux. Zero or multiple matches
                        are refused. Replay/run only: the current Capture path records the local
                        Linux desktop and refuses this flag. Overrides backend.linux_window_title.
  --linux-allow-physical-input
                        Explicitly allow window-bound X11 pointer/keyboard fallback for --backend
                        linux replay/run when native AT-SPI actuation is unavailable. Record
                        refuses this replay-only flag.
  --rdp-host HOST       RDP host/IP for --backend rdp (network RDP via FreeRDP). Overrides
                        backend.rdp_host. Replay/run only: record cannot connect local Capture to
                        this endpoint. Record inside the remote session, or capture a local client
                        with --window/--rdp-window.
  --rdp-window OWNER    Exact local remote-display window owner/process for --backend rdp or
                        citrix. On Windows this is the process basename (for example wfica32); on
                        macOS it is the app owner (for example 'Citrix Viewer'). During record it
                        also scopes local Capture to that window; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.rdp_window.
  --rdp-window-title TITLE
                        Exact local remote-display window title used to disambiguate multiple
                        matching RDP/Citrix client windows. During record it also scopes local
                        Capture; during replay/run it overrides backend.rdp_window_title.
  --rdp-readiness-text TEXT
                        Stable text that must be visible in the current remote frame before input.
                        Required for governed Citrix `run`; overrides backend.rdp_readiness_text.
  --allow-surface-override
                        Explicitly permit executing a workflow on a DIFFERENT surface than the one
                        it was recorded/qualified on (Workflow.surface). Off by default: a cross-
                        surface run is refused. The override is recorded in the run report
                        (surface_override) as compatibility evidence; it is never silent.
  --surface NAME=KIND[:TARGET]
                        Multi-surface bundles: bind a backend to the backend surface NAME
                        (repeatable). KIND defaults to the kind the bundle declares; TARGET fills
                        that kind's target (web: URL, windows: agent URL, macos: app, linux: app,
                        rdp: host, citrix: client window). NAME=TARGET alone is accepted. Other
                        fields go in the config's surfaces: map. Browser tabs and popups need no
                        binding. See docs/MULTI_SURFACE.md.
  --browser-cdp-endpoint URL
                        Run in an already-running, signed-in local Chromium through its loopback
                        DevTools endpoint (for example, http://127.0.0.1:9222) instead of
                        launching a new, signed-out browser. The run binds the one open tab on the
                        --url origin, starts from the screen it shows, and never navigates or
                        closes the browser. Overrides backend.browser_cdp_endpoint from --config.
  --browser-page-url URL
                        Exact current URL of the tab to run in, when more than one open tab has
                        the --url origin. Requires --browser-cdp-endpoint.
  --invocation-challenge INVOCATION_CHALLENGE
                        Non-authority freshness challenge for the local Standard producer.
  --config-sha256 HEX   The SHA-256 of --config's bytes. Flow opens the file once (not through a
                        symlink; it must be a regular file), refuses it if the digest differs, and
                        from then on parses only those bytes whenever this command loads that
                        path, so replacing the file, or a symlink put in its place, changes
                        nothing
  --config YAML         Deployment config YAML wiring backend / actuation / effects / runtime /
                        policy (see docs/deployment.example.yaml). Direct flags below override
                        individual fields.
  --effects-kind {none,rest,fhir,sql,file,document-hash}
                        System-of-record EffectVerifier to wire so consequential writes are
                        verified against the real record (not the screen). rest needs --effects-
                        records-path; the fhir/sql/file kinds need their config fields
                        (resource_type and field_paths, sql_query, root, ...) from a --config
                        deployment YAML
  --effects-base-url EFFECTS_BASE_URL
                        Base URL for the rest / fhir effect verifier
  --effects-records-path EFFECTS_RECORDS_PATH
                        Path whose GET returns the app's records (rest effect verifier)

                        input edge

                        Private signed non-production campaign authority for a resumed
                        qualification input edge
  --url URL             Target app URL to rebuild a live backend (default: backend.url)
  --headed              Run the browser headed
  --roll-back           Instead of resuming, roll the run back with its approved compensations and
                        prove the store matches the read from before the run; also continues a
                        rollback a crash interrupted
  --require-approval    Refuse to resume unless the pending escalation is 'approved' (see
                        `approve`)
  --report              After a successful resume, send the PHI-minimal local completion summary
                        to the paired control plane (also enabled by OPENADAPT_FLOW_REPORT_RUN=1)
  --param K=V           Parameter substitution (repeatable); required again on resume when the
                        effect-verifier config binds run parameters
  --params-file PARAMS_FILE
                        JSON object of parameter bindings; keeps values out of process arguments
                        for managed execution (see --param)
  --backend {web,windows,macos,linux,rdp,citrix}
                        Backend to drive: 'web' (Playwright/Chromium), 'windows' (native Windows
                        via the WAA HTTP agent at replay), 'macos' (one native Mac app window),
                        'linux' (one exact AT-SPI app window at replay), 'rdp' (pixel-only network
                        or local remote desktop), or 'citrix' (the local Citrix Workspace window;
                        its owner defaults by host OS and a configured rdp_window may override
                        it). Overrides backend.kind from --config. Omit on record to capture on
                        this OS, or pass --url to record the browser.
  --agent-url URL       Base URL of the in-guest Windows (WAA) agent for --backend windows (e.g.
                        http://localhost:5001). Replay/run only: desktop record refuses this flag
                        because local Capture cannot bind to a WAA endpoint. Overrides
                        backend.agent_url.
  --macos-app APP       Owner application for --backend macos (e.g. MyApp). During record this
                        scopes Capture to that local app window; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.macos_app.
  --macos-window-title TITLE
                        Window-title substring for --backend macos. Ambiguous matches are refused.
                        During record this scopes Capture; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.macos_window_title.
  --linux-app APP       Exact AT-SPI application name for --backend linux (e.g. gedit). Replay/run
                        only: the current Capture path records the local Linux desktop and refuses
                        this flag. Overrides backend.linux_app.
  --linux-window-title TITLE
                        Exact top-level window title for --backend linux. Zero or multiple matches
                        are refused. Replay/run only: the current Capture path records the local
                        Linux desktop and refuses this flag. Overrides backend.linux_window_title.
  --linux-allow-physical-input
                        Explicitly allow window-bound X11 pointer/keyboard fallback for --backend
                        linux replay/run when native AT-SPI actuation is unavailable. Record
                        refuses this replay-only flag.
  --rdp-host HOST       RDP host/IP for --backend rdp (network RDP via FreeRDP). Overrides
                        backend.rdp_host. Replay/run only: record cannot connect local Capture to
                        this endpoint. Record inside the remote session, or capture a local client
                        with --window/--rdp-window.
  --rdp-window OWNER    Exact local remote-display window owner/process for --backend rdp or
                        citrix. On Windows this is the process basename (for example wfica32); on
                        macOS it is the app owner (for example 'Citrix Viewer'). During record it
                        also scopes local Capture to that window; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.rdp_window.

                        matching RDP/Citrix client windows. During record it also scopes local
                        Capture; during replay/run it overrides backend.rdp_window_title.
  --rdp-readiness-text TEXT
                        Stable text that must be visible in the current remote frame before input.
                        Required for governed Citrix `run`; overrides backend.rdp_readiness_text.
  --allow-surface-override
                        Explicitly permit executing a workflow on a DIFFERENT surface than the one
                        it was recorded/qualified on (Workflow.surface). Off by default: a cross-
                        surface run is refused. The override is recorded in the run report
                        (surface_override) as compatibility evidence; it is never silent.
  --browser-cdp-endpoint URL
                        Run in an already-running, signed-in local Chromium through its loopback
                        DevTools endpoint (for example, http://127.0.0.1:9222) instead of
                        launching a new, signed-out browser. The run binds the one open tab on the
                        --url origin, starts from the screen it shows, and never navigates or
                        closes the browser. Overrides backend.browser_cdp_endpoint from --config.
  --browser-page-url URL

                        the --url origin. Requires --browser-cdp-endpoint.
  --invocation-challenge INVOCATION_CHALLENGE
                        Non-authority freshness challenge for the local Standard producer.
  --config-sha256 HEX   The SHA-256 of --config's bytes. Flow opens the file once (not through a
                        symlink; it must be a regular file), refuses it if the digest differs, and
                        from then on parses only those bytes whenever this command loads that
                        path, so replacing the file, or a symlink put in its place, changes
                        nothing

                        policy (see docs/deployment.example.yaml). Direct flags below override
                        individual fields.
  --effects-kind {none,rest,fhir,sql,file,document-hash}
