                        verified against the real record (not the screen). rest needs --effects-
                        records-path; the fhir/sql/file kinds need their config fields
                        (resource_type and field_paths, sql_query, root, ...) from a --config
                        deployment YAML
  --effects-base-url EFFECTS_BASE_URL
                        Base URL for the rest / fhir effect verifier
  --effects-records-path EFFECTS_RECORDS_PATH
                        Path whose GET returns the app's records (rest effect verifier)
  --effects-root EFFECTS_ROOT
                        Document-store root for the document-hash effect verifier
  --api-actuator        Wire the API/tool actuation tier: a step carrying an ApiBinding is
                        performed via the API (deterministic, $0) and confirmed by the effect
                        verifier, skipping the GUI
  --api-base-url API_BASE_URL
                        Base URL for the API actuator (implies --api-actuator)
  --durable             Enable the Tier-3 durable runtime: checkpoint each verified step and
                        durably PAUSE on halt, so the run is resumable via `resume` (never re-
                        performing a confirmed write)
  --attest-contract PATH
                        OPT-IN: effect-contract YAML for the openadapt-attest proof sidecar. After
                        the run it verifies the claimed effect against the system of record and
                        writes a SIGNED receipt (attest_receipt.json) into the run directory.
                        Never changes the run outcome or exit code. Env fallback:
                        OPENADAPT_FLOW_ATTEST_CONTRACT
  --attest-sign-key PATH
                        Signing key for the attest receipt (env fallback:
                        OPENADAPT_FLOW_ATTEST_SIGN_KEY)
  --attest-audit-log PATH
                        Append-only audit log the attest sidecar writes to (env fallback:
                        OPENADAPT_FLOW_ATTEST_AUDIT_LOG)
  --attest-pre-state PATH
                        Existing pre-actuation system-of-record snapshot for delta checks. When
                        omitted, replay captures one into the run directory
                        (attest_pre_state.json) before actuation begins (env fallback:
                        OPENADAPT_FLOW_ATTEST_PRE_STATE)
  --approver-root HEX   The root approver key (64 hex) this run trusts: a person's answer counts
                        only when its signer is on the signed approver roster this key vouches
                        for. Also set by the deployment config's approvers.root_public_key or
                        OPENADAPT_APPROVER_ROOT; without one, a person's answer is refused
  --key-dir KEY_DIR     Key directory with the signed approver roster (approvers.json) that
                        approvals are checked against; use the one you approved with (default
                        $OPENADAPT_JIT_KEY_DIR or ~/.openadapt/jit)
  --approver-policy FILE
                        A person-signed approver grant (openadapt-flow approver-grant sign): which
                        agents or systems may answer which classes of save, until when. Without a
                        grant that verifies against the signer registry, only a person may answer;
                        an unsigned or tampered file gives no authority. A clinical_write save
                        takes a non-person approver only when the grant's policy pins an opt-in.
  --started-by ID       The agent or system that started this run (opaque id). It can never answer
                        this run's saves. openadapt-agent sets it.
  --approver-webhook URL
                        Ask this https endpoint (the customer's approver agent or system) about
                        each waiting save, with HMAC-signed, PHI-free messages. The secret is read
                        from OPENADAPT_APPROVER_WEBHOOK_SECRET. A person can still answer in
                        Desktop. Needs --approver-webhook-id and a policy that allows the
                        approver's kind.
  --approver-webhook-id APPROVER_WEBHOOK_ID
                        The webhook approver's opaque id, such as system:acme-approvals
  --approver-webhook-kind {agent,system}
                        Whether the webhook approver is an agent or a system (default system)
  --approval-mode {each_item,problems_only,not_gated}
                        Per-item approval before each consequential save. each_item (the default
                        for every run): the run waits before every save until a person approves it
                        in Desktop's Run it (see `item-approval`). problems_only: only problems go
                        to a person; until a switch record is configured, every save still asks.
                        not_gated: no per-item pause, recorded in the report (the hosted runner,
                        Execute and MCP callers). Overrides runtime.approval_mode. A resume always
                        keeps the run's own mode.
  --approval-wait SECONDS
                        How long the run waits for a person's answer before it stops before the
                        save (default 900, at most 14400). An answer given later can still be used
                        by `resume`.

                          [--approval-mode {each_item,problems_only,not_gated}]
                          [--approval-wait SECONDS] [--no-encrypt]

positional arguments:
  bundle                Workflow bundle directory

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --first-screen PNG    Variant sets only: the first screen to route on. Without it the router
                        reads one frame through the selected backend.
  --profile {demo,standard,regulated}
                        Named execution posture (or runtime.profile from --config). Demo is
                        explicitly non-production; Standard requires certification, durability,
                        identity, and independently verified consequential effects. Regulated
                        additionally requires encrypted bundles, strictly sealed evidence assets,
                        and encrypted durable checkpoints in a customer-controlled deployment.
                        Omit only for compatibility with a pre-profile deployment.
  --url URL             Target app URL (default: backend.url from --config)
  --run-dir RUN_DIR     Run output directory (default: runs/replay-<UTC timestamp>)
  --param K=V           Parameter substitution (repeatable)
  --params-file PARAMS_FILE
                        JSON object of parameter bindings; keeps values out of process arguments
                        for managed execution
  --local-grounding     Pixel surfaces (Citrix, RDP, VNC): find icons and unlabeled controls again
                        after a display-scale, zoom, font or theme change with a local model.
                        Look-alikes halt the step. In process, no outbound calls; the pinned 24 MB
                        weights are fetched once.
  --allow-model-grounding
                        EGRESS OPT-IN (PHI audit REM-3): permit wiring an off-box model component
                        (also settable via runtime.allow_model_grounding)
  --save-healed-to SAVE_HEALED_TO
                        Write the healed bundle to this directory
  --headed              Run the browser headed
  --hold-on-halt SECONDS
                        When a browser run halts, keep its page open for up to SECONDS so
                        openadapt-agent can record a repair on it (see
                        openadapt_flow.repair.hold). 0, the default, closes it at once. Max 1800.
  --backend {web,windows,macos,linux,rdp,citrix}
                        Backend to drive: 'web' (Playwright/Chromium), 'windows' (native Windows
                        via the WAA HTTP agent at replay), 'macos' (one native Mac app window),
                        'linux' (one exact AT-SPI app window at replay), 'rdp' (pixel-only network
                        or local remote desktop), or 'citrix' (the local Citrix Workspace window;
                        its owner defaults by host OS and a configured rdp_window may override
                        it). Overrides backend.kind from --config. Omit on record to capture on
                        this OS, or pass --url to record the browser.
  --agent-url URL       Base URL of the in-guest Windows (WAA) agent for --backend windows (e.g.
                        http://localhost:5001). Replay/run only: desktop record refuses this flag
                        because local Capture cannot bind to a WAA endpoint. Overrides
                        backend.agent_url.
  --macos-app APP       Owner application for --backend macos (e.g. MyApp). During record this
                        scopes Capture to that local app window; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.macos_app.
  --macos-window-title TITLE
                        Window-title substring for --backend macos. Ambiguous matches are refused.
                        During record this scopes Capture; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.macos_window_title.
  --linux-app APP       Exact AT-SPI application name for --backend linux (e.g. gedit). Replay/run
                        only: the current Capture path records the local Linux desktop and refuses
                        this flag. Overrides backend.linux_app.
  --linux-window-title TITLE
                        Exact top-level window title for --backend linux. Zero or multiple matches
                        are refused. Replay/run only: the current Capture path records the local
                        Linux desktop and refuses this flag. Overrides backend.linux_window_title.
  --linux-allow-physical-input
                        Explicitly allow window-bound X11 pointer/keyboard fallback for --backend
                        linux replay/run when native AT-SPI actuation is unavailable. Record
                        refuses this replay-only flag.
  --rdp-host HOST       RDP host/IP for --backend rdp (network RDP via FreeRDP). Overrides
                        backend.rdp_host. Replay/run only: record cannot connect local Capture to
                        this endpoint. Record inside the remote session, or capture a local client
                        with --window/--rdp-window.
  --rdp-window OWNER    Exact local remote-display window owner/process for --backend rdp or
                        citrix. On Windows this is the process basename (for example wfica32); on
                        macOS it is the app owner (for example 'Citrix Viewer'). During record it
                        also scopes local Capture to that window; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.rdp_window.
  --rdp-window-title TITLE
                        Exact local remote-display window title used to disambiguate multiple
                        matching RDP/Citrix client windows. During record it also scopes local
                        Capture; during replay/run it overrides backend.rdp_window_title.
  --rdp-readiness-text TEXT
                        Stable text that must be visible in the current remote frame before input.
                        Required for governed Citrix `run`; overrides backend.rdp_readiness_text.
  --allow-surface-override
                        Explicitly permit executing a workflow on a DIFFERENT surface than the one
                        it was recorded/qualified on (Workflow.surface). Off by default: a cross-
                        surface run is refused. The override is recorded in the run report
                        (surface_override) as compatibility evidence; it is never silent.
  --surface NAME=KIND[:TARGET]
                        Multi-surface bundles: bind a backend to the backend surface NAME
                        (repeatable). KIND defaults to the kind the bundle declares; TARGET fills
                        that kind's target (web: URL, windows: agent URL, macos: app, linux: app,
                        rdp: host, citrix: client window). NAME=TARGET alone is accepted. Other
                        fields go in the config's surfaces: map. Browser tabs and popups need no
                        binding. See docs/MULTI_SURFACE.md.
  --browser-cdp-endpoint URL
                        Run in an already-running, signed-in local Chromium through its loopback
                        DevTools endpoint (for example, http://127.0.0.1:9222) instead of
                        launching a new, signed-out browser. The run binds the one open tab on the
                        --url origin, starts from the screen it shows, and never navigates or
                        closes the browser. Overrides backend.browser_cdp_endpoint from --config.
  --browser-page-url URL
                        Exact current URL of the tab to run in, when more than one open tab has
                        the --url origin. Requires --browser-cdp-endpoint.
  --invocation-challenge INVOCATION_CHALLENGE
                        Non-authority freshness challenge for the local Standard producer.
  --config-sha256 HEX   The SHA-256 of --config's bytes. Flow opens the file once (not through a
                        symlink; it must be a regular file), refuses it if the digest differs, and
                        from then on parses only those bytes whenever this command loads that
                        path, so replacing the file, or a symlink put in its place, changes
                        nothing
  --config YAML         Deployment config YAML wiring backend / actuation / effects / runtime /
                        policy (see docs/deployment.example.yaml). Direct flags below override
                        individual fields.
  --effects-kind {none,rest,fhir,sql,file,document-hash}
                        System-of-record EffectVerifier to wire so consequential writes are
                        verified against the real record (not the screen). rest needs --effects-
                        records-path; the fhir/sql/file kinds need their config fields
                        (resource_type and field_paths, sql_query, root, ...) from a --config
                        deployment YAML
  --effects-base-url EFFECTS_BASE_URL
                        Base URL for the rest / fhir effect verifier
  --effects-records-path EFFECTS_RECORDS_PATH
                        Path whose GET returns the app's records (rest effect verifier)
  --effects-root EFFECTS_ROOT
                        Document-store root for the document-hash effect verifier
  --api-actuator        Wire the API/tool actuation tier: a step carrying an ApiBinding is
                        performed via the API (deterministic, $0) and confirmed by the effect
                        verifier, skipping the GUI
  --api-base-url API_BASE_URL
                        Base URL for the API actuator (implies --api-actuator)
  --durable             Enable the Tier-3 durable runtime: checkpoint each verified step and
                        durably PAUSE on halt, so the run is resumable via `resume` (never re-
                        performing a confirmed write)
  --worklist [RELATION=]FILE
                        CSV/JSON worklist of parameter rows driving a PROGRAM bundle's loop over a
                        relation (repeatable). 'RELATION=FILE' binds the file to that relation; a
                        bare 'FILE' binds to the program's sole loop relation.
  --workers N           Run a worklist program's items on N workers at once, each in its own
                        signed-in session (docs/THROUGHPUT.md). The deployment must declare
                        worklist.max_workers >= N, one account per worker, and items_independent:
                        true. Each item is claimed once; a halt on any worker stops new items on
                        all of them.
  --readback-window K   Let a worker start its next item while up to K earlier saves still wait
                        for their system-of-record read-back (default: worklist.readback_window,
                        normally 0). A failed read-back stops the run and names the items written
                        after it.
  --attest-contract PATH
                        OPT-IN: effect-contract YAML for the openadapt-attest proof sidecar. After
                        the run it verifies the claimed effect against the system of record and
                        writes a SIGNED receipt (attest_receipt.json) into the run directory.
                        Never changes the run outcome or exit code. Env fallback:
                        OPENADAPT_FLOW_ATTEST_CONTRACT
  --attest-sign-key PATH
                        Signing key for the attest receipt (env fallback:
                        OPENADAPT_FLOW_ATTEST_SIGN_KEY)
  --attest-audit-log PATH
                        Append-only audit log the attest sidecar writes to (env fallback:
                        OPENADAPT_FLOW_ATTEST_AUDIT_LOG)
  --attest-pre-state PATH
                        Existing pre-actuation system-of-record snapshot for delta checks. When
                        omitted, replay captures one into the run directory
                        (attest_pre_state.json) before actuation begins (env fallback:
                        OPENADAPT_FLOW_ATTEST_PRE_STATE)
  --policy NAME-OR-PATH
                        Certifying policy the bundle must PASS to run (default: the deployment
                        config's policy, else 'clinical-write')
  --approve-unverified-writes
                        APPROVAL FALLBACK: explicitly approve executing writes whose effects
                        cannot be independently verified in this deployment (no verifier
                        configured). Without it such a bundle is refused
  --strict-templates    Refuse (not just warn) when template/screenshot assets are unsealed
                        (plaintext at rest)
  --allow-unencrypted   Escape hatch: permit running a bundle whose workflow.json is NOT encrypted
                        at rest (disables the encryption gate). Discouraged
  --pin-digest SHA256   Refuse unless the bundle's sealed content digest equals this
  --pin-version VERSION
                        Refuse unless the bundle's compiler version equals this
  --subroutine-library JSON
                        Current subroutine library to re-admit embedded subroutines against before
                        this run. Required when the bundle embeds a subroutine; a certification
                        made before a newer version was published does not let the old version
                        run.
  --subroutine-workflow-id ID
                        Id this workflow was registered under when it was certified (default: the
                        workflow name)
  --permission-trust PATH, --qualification-trust PATH
                        Trusted signers for process run permissions. Also
                        OPENADAPT_QUALIFICATION_TRUST or qualification-trust.json beside process-
                        contract.json. --qualification-trust is deprecated; use --permission-
                        trust.
  --execute-url URL     HTTPS Execute v1 base URL for process children (OPENADAPT_EXECUTE_URL).
                        Local process run uses governed run unless this and a bearer token are set
  --execute-environment-id ID
                        Execute environment_id for process children
                        (OPENADAPT_EXECUTE_ENVIRONMENT_ID)
  --code-trust PATH     Code-admission Ed25519 signer registry for ProcessContract v1. Required
                        when the contract contains a code child.
  --code-runtime-environment-digest SHA256
                        Exact admitted runtime-environment digest for code children
  --allow-trusted-code  Approve exact admitted code that uses the trusted_local profile
  --process-receipt-private-key PATH
                        Raw 32-byte Ed25519 key for the ProcessContract v1 terminal receipt
  --process-receipt-issuer-key-id PROCESS_RECEIPT_ISSUER_KEY_ID
  --process-environment-id PROCESS_ENVIRONMENT_ID
  --process-runner-id PROCESS_RUNNER_ID
  --qualification-authority-file PATH
                        Private owner-only Production qualification authority (v2 envelope or
                        issued openadapt.qualification-admission/v4). Required for Standard and
                        Regulated actuation; verified and re-read at every input edge
  --dry-run, --explain  Print the fail-closed coverage report and exit WITHOUT executing
  --report              OPT-IN: after a SUCCESSFUL run, emit the PHI-free run summary to the
                        paired hosted control plane (see `report-run`). Off by default — nothing
                        is ever uploaded without this flag (or OPENADAPT_FLOW_REPORT_RUN=1)
  --cloud-execution-id CLOUD_EXECUTION_ID
                        OpenAdapt Cloud Execute execution this run belongs to (or
                        OPENADAPT_CLOUD_EXECUTION_ID). After a VERIFIED outcome, Cloud's signed
                        receipt is fetched with OPENADAPT_EXECUTE_API_KEY and written into
                        report.json as execute_receipt.
  --approver-root HEX   The root approver key (64 hex) this run trusts: a person's answer counts
                        only when its signer is on the signed approver roster this key vouches
                        for. Also set by the deployment config's approvers.root_public_key or
                        OPENADAPT_APPROVER_ROOT; without one, a person's answer is refused
  --key-dir KEY_DIR     Key directory with the signed approver roster (approvers.json) that
                        approvals are checked against; use the one you approved with (default
                        $OPENADAPT_JIT_KEY_DIR or ~/.openadapt/jit)
  --approver-policy FILE
                        A person-signed approver grant (openadapt-flow approver-grant sign): which
                        agents or systems may answer which classes of save, until when. Without a
                        grant that verifies against the signer registry, only a person may answer;
                        an unsigned or tampered file gives no authority. A clinical_write save
                        takes a non-person approver only when the grant's policy pins an opt-in.
  --started-by ID       The agent or system that started this run (opaque id). It can never answer
                        this run's saves. openadapt-agent sets it.
  --approver-webhook URL
                        Ask this https endpoint (the customer's approver agent or system) about
                        each waiting save, with HMAC-signed, PHI-free messages. The secret is read
                        from OPENADAPT_APPROVER_WEBHOOK_SECRET. A person can still answer in
                        Desktop. Needs --approver-webhook-id and a policy that allows the
                        approver's kind.
  --approver-webhook-id APPROVER_WEBHOOK_ID
                        The webhook approver's opaque id, such as system:acme-approvals
  --approver-webhook-kind {agent,system}
                        Whether the webhook approver is an agent or a system (default system)
  --approval-mode {each_item,problems_only,not_gated}
                        Per-item approval before each consequential save. each_item (the default
                        for every run): the run waits before every save until a person approves it
                        in Desktop's Run it (see `item-approval`). problems_only: only problems go
                        to a person; until a switch record is configured, every save still asks.
                        not_gated: no per-item pause, recorded in the report (the hosted runner,
                        Execute and MCP callers). Overrides runtime.approval_mode. A resume always
                        keeps the run's own mode.
  --approval-wait SECONDS
                        How long the run waits for a person's answer before it stops before the
                        save (default 900, at most 14400). An answer given later can still be used
                        by `resume`.
  --no-encrypt          Write this command's output in plaintext (recorded in
                        ~/.openadapt/plaintext-at-rest.jsonl, with a warning). Output is encrypted
                        by default; same as OPENADAPT_ENCRYPT_AT_REST=0. Ignored under
                        OPENADAPT_FLOW_AT_REST=strict

self-repair:
  When the run halts before any effect because a screen changed, a repair agent proposes a fix,
  Flow probes it up to the save, and one person approves it before the run resumes. On by
  default whenever a repair agent is configured (here or in the deployment file's repair
  section). See docs/SELF_REPAIR.md.

  --self-repair         Require self-repair for this run (web runs against --url): refuse the run
                        when it can't be repaired.
  --no-auto-repair      Do not hand stops to the repair agent; a stop waits for a person.
  --repair-agent MODULE:NAME
                        The repair agent: an object, class or factory with dialect, agent_id and
                        propose(request).
  --repair-screen-access-by NAME
                        The person who allowed the agent to see screens (recorded).
  --repair-screen-share-mode {scrubbed_only,allow_unscrubbed}
                        Scrub screens before the agent sees them (default) or not.
  --repair-model-provider {anthropic,openai}
                        Load the customer's own key for an agent that calls a model.
  --repair-model-key-file PATH
                        The customer's key file ({"anthropic": {"api_key": ...}}).
  --repair-store REPAIR_STORE
                        The repair store the candidate enters (default repair-store/).
  --repair-attempts REPAIR_ATTEMPTS
                        Proposals tried for one halt (default 3).
  --repair-fault-url URL
                        A URL that presents a fault the patched run must refuse before the save
                        (repeatable). Needed when the step's identity is read from the DOM.
  --repair-approval-wait SECONDS
                        How long to wait for a person's answer (default 900).

help.openadapt-flow scaffold-verifier:
usage: openadapt-flow scaffold-verifier [-h] [-o DIR] [--db SQLITE] [--verifier YAML]
                                        [--prove FIXTURE] [--complete-read] [--fault-gate]
                                        [--probe-reads] [--probe-base URL] [--recording DIR]
                                        [--bundle DIR]
                                        source

positional arguments:
  source             Recording directory OR workflow bundle directory

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  -o DIR, --out DIR  Directory for the proposed check or drafted effect_contract.yaml (default:
                     beside the input)
  --db SQLITE        Read-only database read path (SQLite file): find the saved row in every table
                     and guard the rest with a no-new-rows check
  --verifier YAML    A verify.yaml whose `verifier:` section reads the system of record (REST,
                     FHIR, SQL); read once to find the saved record
  --prove FIXTURE    Also run the proposed check end to end against this caller-supplied fault
                     fixture (requires an injected proof source)
  --complete-read    Declare that the reads return everything the save can change (one store, no
                     other tables). Recorded as declared, not proven
  --fault-gate       With --db: write each bad save to a copy of the database and let the check
                     read it through its own read (the fault gate). A fault the read can't see
                     keeps the check a draft
  --probe-reads      When the recording never reads the saved record back, derive reads from the
                     captured write and probe them with GET on a local copy of the app; use one
                     only when it returns the written values. Every probe is recorded in the proof
  --probe-base URL   With --probe-reads: the local copy of the app to probe (default: the recorded
                     origin, which must be the local machine)
  --recording DIR    The recording a bundle was compiled from (when SOURCE is a bundle)
  --bundle DIR       The bundle compiled from this recording, for identity coverage (when SOURCE
                     is a recording)

Also available as: openadapt-flow compile --scaffold-verifier

model from the save, the recorded form structure, the fields and any narration. They are display
metadata; execution ignores them and they are outside the bundle digests, so editing them never
changes a certification.

usage: openadapt-flow undo run [-h] --bundle BUNDLE --undo UNDO_ID [--url URL] [--headed]
                               [--backend {web,windows,macos,linux,rdp,citrix}] [--agent-url URL]
                               [--macos-app APP] [--macos-window-title TITLE] [--linux-app APP]
                               [--linux-window-title TITLE] [--linux-allow-physical-input]
                               [--rdp-host HOST] [--rdp-window OWNER] [--rdp-window-title TITLE]
                               [--rdp-readiness-text TEXT] [--allow-surface-override]
                               [--browser-cdp-endpoint URL] [--browser-page-url URL]
                               [--invocation-challenge INVOCATION_CHALLENGE] [--config-sha256 HEX]
                               [--config YAML]
                               [--effects-kind {none,rest,fhir,sql,file,document-hash}]
                               [--effects-base-url EFFECTS_BASE_URL]
                               [--effects-records-path EFFECTS_RECORDS_PATH]
                               [--effects-root EFFECTS_ROOT] [--api-actuator]
                               [--api-base-url API_BASE_URL] [--durable]
                               run_dir

positional arguments:
  run_dir               The stopped run's directory

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --bundle BUNDLE       The run's bundle directory
  --undo UNDO_ID        Undo id
  --url URL             URL of the target app (required unless the config names one)
  --headed              Run the browser headed
  --backend {web,windows,macos,linux,rdp,citrix}
                        Backend to drive: 'web' (Playwright/Chromium), 'windows' (native Windows
                        via the WAA HTTP agent at replay), 'macos' (one native Mac app window),
                        'linux' (one exact AT-SPI app window at replay), 'rdp' (pixel-only network
                        or local remote desktop), or 'citrix' (the local Citrix Workspace window;
                        its owner defaults by host OS and a configured rdp_window may override
                        it). Overrides backend.kind from --config. Omit on record to capture on
                        this OS, or pass --url to record the browser.
  --agent-url URL       Base URL of the in-guest Windows (WAA) agent for --backend windows (e.g.
                        http://localhost:5001). Replay/run only: desktop record refuses this flag
                        because local Capture cannot bind to a WAA endpoint. Overrides
                        backend.agent_url.
  --macos-app APP       Owner application for --backend macos (e.g. MyApp). During record this
                        scopes Capture to that local app window; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.macos_app.
  --macos-window-title TITLE
                        Window-title substring for --backend macos. Ambiguous matches are refused.
                        During record this scopes Capture; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.macos_window_title.
  --linux-app APP       Exact AT-SPI application name for --backend linux (e.g. gedit). Replay/run
                        only: the current Capture path records the local Linux desktop and refuses
                        this flag. Overrides backend.linux_app.
  --linux-window-title TITLE
                        Exact top-level window title for --backend linux. Zero or multiple matches
                        are refused. Replay/run only: the current Capture path records the local
                        Linux desktop and refuses this flag. Overrides backend.linux_window_title.
  --linux-allow-physical-input
                        Explicitly allow window-bound X11 pointer/keyboard fallback for --backend
                        linux replay/run when native AT-SPI actuation is unavailable. Record
                        refuses this replay-only flag.
  --rdp-host HOST       RDP host/IP for --backend rdp (network RDP via FreeRDP). Overrides
                        backend.rdp_host. Replay/run only: record cannot connect local Capture to
                        this endpoint. Record inside the remote session, or capture a local client
                        with --window/--rdp-window.
  --rdp-window OWNER    Exact local remote-display window owner/process for --backend rdp or
                        citrix. On Windows this is the process basename (for example wfica32); on
                        macOS it is the app owner (for example 'Citrix Viewer'). During record it
                        also scopes local Capture to that window; during replay/run it overrides
                        backend.rdp_window.
  --rdp-window-title TITLE
                        Exact local remote-display window title used to disambiguate multiple
                        matching RDP/Citrix client windows. During record it also scopes local
                        Capture; during replay/run it overrides backend.rdp_window_title.
  --rdp-readiness-text TEXT
                        Stable text that must be visible in the current remote frame before input.
                        Required for governed Citrix `run`; overrides backend.rdp_readiness_text.
  --allow-surface-override
                        Explicitly permit executing a workflow on a DIFFERENT surface than the one
                        it was recorded/qualified on (Workflow.surface). Off by default: a cross-
                        surface run is refused. The override is recorded in the run report
                        (surface_override) as compatibility evidence; it is never silent.
  --browser-cdp-endpoint URL
                        Run in an already-running, signed-in local Chromium through its loopback
                        DevTools endpoint (for example, http://127.0.0.1:9222) instead of
                        launching a new, signed-out browser. The run binds the one open tab on the
                        --url origin, starts from the screen it shows, and never navigates or
                        closes the browser. Overrides backend.browser_cdp_endpoint from --config.
  --browser-page-url URL
                        Exact current URL of the tab to run in, when more than one open tab has
                        the --url origin. Requires --browser-cdp-endpoint.
  --invocation-challenge INVOCATION_CHALLENGE
                        Non-authority freshness challenge for the local Standard producer.
  --config-sha256 HEX   The SHA-256 of --config's bytes. Flow opens the file once (not through a
                        symlink; it must be a regular file), refuses it if the digest differs, and
                        from then on parses only those bytes whenever this command loads that
                        path, so replacing the file, or a symlink put in its place, changes
                        nothing
  --config YAML         Deployment config YAML wiring backend / actuation / effects / runtime /
                        policy (see docs/deployment.example.yaml). Direct flags below override
                        individual fields.
  --effects-kind {none,rest,fhir,sql,file,document-hash}
                        System-of-record EffectVerifier to wire so consequential writes are
                        verified against the real record (not the screen). rest needs --effects-
                        records-path; the fhir/sql/file kinds need their config fields
                        (resource_type and field_paths, sql_query, root, ...) from a --config
                        deployment YAML
  --effects-base-url EFFECTS_BASE_URL
                        Base URL for the rest / fhir effect verifier
  --effects-records-path EFFECTS_RECORDS_PATH
                        Path whose GET returns the app's records (rest effect verifier)
  --effects-root EFFECTS_ROOT
                        Document-store root for the document-hash effect verifier
  --api-actuator        Wire the API/tool actuation tier: a step carrying an ApiBinding is
                        performed via the API (deterministic, $0) and confirmed by the effect
                        verifier, skipping the GUI
  --api-base-url API_BASE_URL
                        Base URL for the API actuator (implies --api-actuator)
  --durable             Enable the Tier-3 durable runtime: checkpoint each verified step and
                        durably PAUSE on halt, so the run is resumable via `resume` (never re-
                        performing a confirmed write)
